Sentence (English): I feel like the time I spent debating whether or not to get a dishwasher during my remodeling was a waste.
Comments (English): I feel like the time I spent debating whether or not to get a dishwasher during my remodeling was a waste. After running it every day for about a month, I truly understand why everyone says "dishwashers are love." First off, the design is the finishing touch to the kitchen. I matched the color to my lower cabinets, and it fits perfectly, looking just like a built-in unit; I feel so pleased every time I look at it. The unique matte finish of the Objet Collection is luxurious and really brightens up the kitchen atmosphere. What I am most satisfied with is, of course, the cleaning power. Since my kids are 5 and 2 years old, we have a pile of burnt-on rice and greasy plates after meals, but even if I just roughly pre-wash them, they come out squeaky clean, perhaps thanks to the Tornado washing blades. The 100% True Steam function is especially reassuring. It gives me peace of mind knowing I don't need to separately sterilize baby bottles or tableware. And the automatic door opening feature! This is really important. After the wash is finished, the door opens slightly to completely blow away the internal moisture, so I don't have to worry about odors, and drying is much faster. Since I can just run it before going to bed at night and tidy up when I wake up in the morning, my mornings have become much more relaxed.
Comments (Original): 리모델링하면서 식기세척기 넣을까 말까 고민했던 시간이 아까울 정도네요. 한 달 정도 매일 돌려보니 왜 다들 '식세기는 사랑'이라고 하는지 뼈저리게 느끼고 있습니다.​일단 디자인부터가 주방의 완성이에요. 저희 집 주방 하부장이랑 컬러를 맞췄더니 빌트인처럼 깔끔하게 딱 떨어지는데, 볼 때마다 흐뭇합니다. 오브제컬렉션 특유의 무광 느낌이 고급스러워서 주방 분위기가 확 살더라고요.​가장 만족스러운 건 역시 세척력입니다. 애들이 5살, 2살이라 밥 먹고 나면 눌러붙은 밥알이나 기름기 있는 식판이 한가득인데, 애벌설거지 대충 해서 넣어도 토네이도 세척날개 덕분인지 아주 뽀득뽀득하게 닦여 나와요. 특히 100℃ 트루스팀 기능은 정말 안심이 됩니다. 아이들 젖병이나 식기류 살균 소독이 따로 필요 없어서 마음이 놓이더라고요.​그리고 자동 문 열림 기능! 이거 진짜 중요합니다. 세척 끝나고 문이 살짝 열리면서 내부 습기를 싹 날려주니까 냄새 걱정도 없고 건조도 훨씬 빨라요. 밤에 자기 전에 돌려놓고 아침에 일어나서 정리만 하면 되니까 아침 시간이 훨씬 여유로워졌습니다.

After running it every day for about a month, I truly understand why everyone says "dishwashers are love." First off, the design is the finishing touch to the kitchen. I matched the color to my lower cabinets, and it fits perfectly, looking just like a built-in unit; I feel so pleased every time I look at it. The unique matte finish of the Objet Collection is luxurious and really brightens up the kitchen atmosphere. What I am most satisfied with is, of course, the cleaning power. Since my kids are 5 and 2 years old, we have a pile of burnt-on rice and greasy plates after meals, but even if I just roughly pre-wash them, they come out squeaky clean, perhaps thanks to the Tornado washing blades. The 100% True Steam function is especially reassuring. It gives me peace of mind knowing I don't need to separately sterilize baby bottles or tableware. And the automatic door opening feature! This is really important. After the wash is finished, the door opens slightly to completely blow away the internal moisture, so I don't have to worry about odors, and drying is much faster. Since I can just run it before going to bed at night and tidy up when I wake up in the morning, my mornings have become much more relaxed.
Comments (Original): 리모델링하면서 식기세척기 넣을까 말까 고민했던 시간이 아까울 정도네요. 한 달 정도 매일 돌려보니 왜 다들 '식세기는 사랑'이라고 하는지 뼈저리게 느끼고 있습니다.​일단 디자인부터가 주방의 완성이에요. 저희 집 주방 하부장이랑 컬러를 맞췄더니 빌트인처럼 깔끔하게 딱 떨어지는데, 볼 때마다 흐뭇합니다. 오브제컬렉션 특유의 무광 느낌이 고급스러워서 주방 분위기가 확 살더라고요.​가장 만족스러운 건 역시 세척력입니다. 애들이 5살, 2살이라 밥 먹고 나면 눌러붙은 밥알이나 기름기 있는 식판이 한가득인데, 애벌설거지 대충 해서 넣어도 토네이도 세척날개 덕분인지 아주 뽀득뽀득하게 닦여 나와요. 특히 100℃ 트루스팀 기능은 정말 안심이 됩니다. 아이들 젖병이나 식기류 살균 소독이 따로 필요 없어서 마음이 놓이더라고요.​그리고 자동 문 열림 기능! 이거 진짜 중요합니다. 세척 끝나고 문이 살짝 열리면서 내부 습기를 싹 날려주니까 냄새 걱정도 없고 건조도 훨씬 빨라요. 밤에 자기 전에 돌려놓고 아침에 일어나서 정리만 하면 되니까 아침 시간이 훨씬 여유로워졌습니다.

Sentence (English): I've been using it for over 20 years.
Comments (English): I've been using it for over 20 years. You shouldn't trust dishwashers too much. Grilled fish dishes? I absolutely never put them in. Since they are sealed and washed with hot water, all the odors get shared. When I first used it, I ran a bowl of soybean paste stew in it, and I suffered for a while because of the smell. Of course, it can't compare to scrubbing them thoroughly by hand. I don't put greasy items or dishes from strong-smelling food in it. I hand-wash cups and cutlery that touch my mouth, but if I'm feeling lazy, I sometimes put them in the dishwasher; however, I make sure to wash them with detergent and rinse them, even if just roughly. If I get messy, I seal the trash can and do the dishes inside.
Comments (Original): 20년 넘게 쓰고 있어요.식세기를 너무 믿으심 안 돼요.생선구이 그릇? 저는 절대 안 넣어요.밀폐해 놓고 뜨거운 물로 세척하는 거라 냄새 다 공유됩니다. 처음 쓸 때 된장찌개 그릇 돌렸다가 냄새 나서 한동안 고생.손으로 빡빡 문질러 닦는 것만 당연 못하죠.기름기 있는 것, 냄새 강한 음식 그릇, 안 넣어요. 입에 닿는 컵이나 수저류는 손으로 닦지만 귀찮으면 넣기도 하는데요, 대충이라도 세제로 닦고 헹궈서 넣어요. 지저분하게 쓰면 쓰레기통 밀폐해 놓고 설거지하는 거. ㅠㅠ

Sentence (English): The first few months were fine, but then I started having a lot of trouble.
Comments (English): [ Nothing but problems 5 months in. ] || ---------------- || The first few months were fine, but then I started having a lot of trouble. GE told the tech to tell me to not have chunks of food left on the plates, which I do not anyway, and again how about those coffee rings? I also have found two factory mounting screws that were dropped within the dishwasher and came out months later sitting on the bottom of my stainless steel tub and left a rust mark. How is that possible? WORST dishwasher ever and I am now done with GE. I will never recommend them.

Sentence (English): We got this model because it has a water softener.
Comments (English): [ Nice quiet dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We got this model because it has a water softener. Our water is quite hard. The dishwasher does an excellent job of cleaning the dishes. It is so quiet that we can run it 20 feet from where we are watching TV and not have the show interrupted. This model comes with a smartphone app that lets you control option, do delayed starts, and otherwise configure the dishwasher. Probably because of the app there are fewer physical controls on this model than on our previous Bosch dishwasher. This means you MUST use the app to do certain things. For instance ECO mode and Half Load are only selectable via the app. Same for various delayed starts. (There is a really nice delayed start setting that lets you pick optimum hours to run the dishwasher and selects the closest window to when you initiate the delayed start.) There is a downside to this, though. The app has been rather tempromental for me. Sometimes for no apparent reason the app cannot connect to the dishwasher. Other times it will connect and perform some functions but will not successfully initiate a delalyed start. When one of these failures occurs the only way to get things working again is to get the dishwasher to reset. Sometimes the on button reset gets things back to normal. But sometimes it is necessary to remove power from the dishwasher for 15 minmutes. So if the failure occurs when you are in a hurry to set some app option and get the dishes done you are out of luck;

Comments (English): [ The best filial piety appliances for your mother ] || ---------------- || Powerful, thorough cleaning with 54 water jets. Water softening minimizes stains on glass cups. Automatic door opening ensures fresh, dry drying. Built-in design creates a neat kitchen. Reason for purchase: For my mother, who often suffers from wrist pain and struggles while doing the dishes. I wanted to lighten the burden of housework as a birthday gift, so after much consideration, I decided to get a dishwasher. I bought it with the hope of reducing the time spent on the daily repetitive dishwashing and allowing her to rest more comfortably! Guaranteed cleaning power with 54 three-dimensional water jets. A total of 54 water jets are sprayed, including the upper sprinkler, the middle wide washing blade, and the lower tornado washing blade. The water covers each dish as if enveloping it, ensuring no blind spots are missed and cleanly removing even stubborn food residue and grease. It feels even cleaner than hand washing, so once you use it, it is hard to go back. Clean without water stains thanks to the water softening system. Almost no white marks remain on glass cups or dishes even after drying. My mother particularly loves that she can see the cleanliness of clear cups or stainless steel dishes when they are taken out. The hassle of wiping water separately has been reduced, making post-use maintenance much easier. Perfect finish with automatic door opening drying. Once washing is finished, the door opens automatically, allowing internal moisture to escape quickly. Thanks to this feature, no water remains, allowing for natural drying to ensure a much fresher finish. The drying performance is so reliable that you can store your dishes immediately. Safe use with temperature detection. The door is designed to open only when the temperature drops below a certain level, so it won't suddenly open while hot. It is safely designed for use both during and immediately after use, so you can use it with peace of mind. Spacious interior for storing various dishes. As it is a 12-place setting, large pots and pans fit comfortably, and you can organize plates, cups, and cutlery all at once. The shelf structure is well-divided, allowing you to stably arrange dishes by type and making it easy to organize while using the dishwasher. Sentence (English): My dishwashing stress is over!
Comments (English): [ It is the moment you are freed from washing dishes. ] || ---------------- || My dishwashing stress is over! I am truly satisfied with the LG Dios Objet 14-place setting dishwasher. I agonized over which dishwasher to buy for a very long time before finally choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-place setting. Since it is a pricey product, I debated a lot about whether to buy it or not. To start with the conclusion, I am so satisfied that I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. In the past, just having a pile of dishes was stressful in itself. I hated doing it even more on days when I ate greasy food. But now, I just put everything in, press a button, and that's it. My life has become so much more convenient. The most satisfying part is the 100°C TrueSteam sterilization wash. Even when I am concerned about hygiene, like with my child's dishes, knowing that they are being cleaned with high-temperature steam gives me much more peace of mind. I am highly satisfied because it feels like it goes beyond simply getting clean and actually sterilizes. Also, perhaps because it is a 14-place setting model, the capacity is really generous. Pots and pans fit in all at once, so there is no need to split the washing up. Before, having a sink overflowing was a daily routine, but now that everything is organized at once, the kitchen looks much neater. The cleaning power is better than expected. Even greasy dishes come out clean without needing much pre-washing, which is satisfying. Since it dries neatly as well, I can just take them out and put them away immediately, so it requires almost no effort. As expected from the Objet Collection, the design has a clean feel that doesn't detract from the kitchen interior. Being built-in, it feels more organized, and the overall atmosphere of the kitchen feels upgraded. What I realized while using it is that this isn't just a simple appliance, but a product that saves time. Since dishwashing time is reduced, I can use that time to rest or do other things, so my quality of life has definitely improved. Overall, if you are considering buying a dishwasher, this is a product I can highly recommend. I think satisfaction will be much higher, especially for families or those who want to reduce dishwashing stress. It also has an automatic door opening feature, so it is a smart product that requires absolutely no attention. I was debating between similar products before buying this one, but I think I made the right choice in selecting this one.

Good service all along the way (sales, customer service and finance) from Leon's. I would definitely buy again from Leons. Only area of improvement: I received two different mailed thank you cards: first one was when I was waiting for my replacement dishwasher to arrive and be installed. I received $50 off the regular price, and eventually, after my follow-up request, received another $50 off due to a lower price offered at Leons. I was replacing my 18 year old Whirlpool Gold, two rack dishwasher which I loved. I considered LG, Samsung and Whirlpool after much research and watching prices go up and up due to tariffs on this American made model over many months. The first dishwasher came damaged from the manufacturer with 2 vertical scratches and one dent on the front door. Leon's immediately triggered an exchange. My second dishwasher arrived September 2025: it's been 7 months now and no complaints. It's beautiful, love the handle, I love the larger 3rd rack which has a rack on one side to pull in and out. It holds a variety of low height items (plastic containers, small bowls, short cups, plastic utensils) Definately have more space in this dishwasher. The cutlery tray on the main rack is fabulous: enabling speedy organization of cutlery. The second rack lifts up and down depending how much height you need. Shorter cookie sheets fit nicely on the main rack (when the minimum height is used). After you select which cycle and press Start, you have four seconds to close the door which is ample time. I have only tried Normal and Sensor cycles with Air Dry. The Sensor washing setting, which is about 3.5 hours, works no better than the Normal cycle (1.5 hours). I always use air dry, to save energy, where the door automatically opens up. I find the Sensor cycle always takes the same amount of time (no sensing or difference for me). Even with a well-stacked full load, the Normal cycle is just fine. When on, there is a small light that is on on the upper right corner of the door. Sound is non-existent: you can't hear my DB39 dishwasher cleaning, which is a big upgrade from the "Boom. Swish" of my past one. Cascade Platinum Plus Actionpacs work best, and I prefer them over Finish pellets. I don't use a rinse aid. I have the Heat Dry setting on at all times: the machine remembers that you had used this previously. What it doesn't save, however, is the washing Cycle: it always defaults to the Sensor cycle. I wish it too would remember the last wash cycle. I find vinegar and water is the best way to clean my stainless steel door appliances.I would definately buy a Whirlpool dishwasher and with Leon's again.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.
