Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Sentence (English): The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished.
Comments (English): [ The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly gold. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

Feeding, playing... ] || ---------------- || The biggest thing I’ve realized while parenting lately is that time is truly money. Anyone who has raised a baby will understand, but the day just flies by in a flash. You have to feed them, play with them, put them to sleep, and do housework in between. Among those tasks, washing dishes feels the hardest because it is repetitive labor every single day. We were originally of the opinion that we could manage without a dishwasher. We thought, "Washing dishes is quick, isn't it? We don't have that many dishes, so it should be fine." But after the baby was born, the situation changed completely. First off, there are the bottles. You know how many times a day you have to wash them, right? Then, when you start solid foods, the number of containers, spoons, and blender cups increases. Toys are put in the mouth, so they need to be washed frequently too. As they piled up one by one, the sink always felt like something was stacked up. The hardest part was at night. I’m completely exhausted after putting the kids to bed, but when I see the pile of dishes in the sink... the moment I see them, it feels like my energy drops by 50. My first thought was, "Do I have to do this again?" So, after much deliberation, I finally bought a dishwasher. To start with the conclusion, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner. Hesitating only delays things. My quality of life has completely changed since I got a dishwasher. It’s not just a matter of convenience; it feels almost like an essential item for a household with young children. First of all, the best thing is that everything gets processed in one go. I don't have to wash dishes immediately; I just have to put them away after use. It gives me so much peace of mind. The same goes for baby bottles. When I washed them by hand, I used to worry if they weren't cleaned thoroughly enough. But now that I put them in the dishwasher, they feel much more hygienically maintained. I also feel reassured because it washes at a high temperature. The same goes for toys, especially the ones that go in the mouth. Washing them separately every time used to be a chore, but now I can just put them in together and run the cycle, which is so convenient. Also, the cleaning power is actually better than I expected. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I wondered, "Isn't washing by hand cleaner?" But even greasy dishes come off cleanly, and I can barely see any water stains left on cups. I am also satisfied with the drying function. Before, wiping the water off after washing and organizing the drying rack—that process itself was a chore. It’s so convenient now because I just have to take everything out when it’s finished. And personally, the best moment was after putting the kids to bed. In the past, the routine was to just think, "Okay, let's rest," see the pile of dishes in the sink, and start working again. But now, I just put everything in, press one button, and it’s done. That really makes a huge difference. I now have the leisure to just sit and rest, talk with my wife, or laugh while looking at pictures of the baby. When raising children, physical stamina is important, but having mental space is truly crucial. It feels like the dishwasher is fulfilling that role. It’s also good for our relationship (?). We don't have to worry about who does the dishes anymore. Since we just put everything in and run it, unnecessary stress has disappeared. Honestly, I know many of you are hesitating because of the price, but I think you should think of this not as an appliance, but as a tool that buys time. Especially for households with babies, it feels less like simple convenience and more like a necessity. To summarize: it can wash baby bottles, baby food containers, and toys all at once. High-temperature washing reduces hygiene concerns. The stress of washing dishes itself has vanished. Improved quality of life after putting the kids to bed. Reduced marital conflict(?). Satisfied with both cleaning and drying power, better than expected. To put it in just one sentence... it is like a ray of light for those of us exhausted by childcare. If you are currently hesitating, I will tell you with all sincerity: hesitating only delays things. Don't regret buying it late like I did. Get it as soon as possible.

If you are not careful, the dishes might not be cleaned properly or there might be detergent residue left behind. ] || ---------------- || First off, I was a bit frustrated because there weren't any specific videos or guides on how to arrange the dishes in the dishwasher when I first started using it. I went through some trial and error, sometimes finding that the dishes weren't cleaned properly or that detergent remained, but now I think I've adapted to a somewhat efficient arrangement. Since the water sprays more strongly from the bottom, it is difficult to place pots on top of the dishes, and because we use a lot of dishes for a two-person household, there are times when I can't even fit a pot in at all. Proper arrangement ensures better drying. Once the wash is finished, I manually rotate the upper washing blades a few times to shake off any remaining water. A surprising amount of water drips down! Even if I only open the door slightly, about 80% of the dishes dry, but if I open it completely and pull the basket forward, they dry much faster, so I don't find it particularly inconvenient even without the hot air drying function. Because I am a meticulous person, the pre-washing process takes more time than expected as I try to remove even the rice grains stuck to the spoons. Still, I feel it is much better than cleaning up food residue later. Regardless, it is definitely convenient once the dishwasher is running. The noise level isn't as quiet as I expected, though. It’s a bit surprising when you first turn it on, and sometimes it even feels bigger than a wash tower. However, I’m gradually getting used to it as I use it. The actual size is much larger and it has a substantial presence. I usually use the standard mode, but the powerful course feels like it removes grease better, perhaps because of the higher temperature. Sentence (English): (This review was collected as part of a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ Cleans well despite confusing button behaviour ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) This WiFi enabled dishwasher cleans well however to access all the features it requires usage of the Home Connect APP which is hit or miss. If you don't want to be struggling with advanced features best to buy a model without the online connectivity so that the dishwasher can be controlled properly using the front panel buttons. The dishwasher seems to be working OK now after spending many hours trying to figure out why it would not complete the wash cycle, often resulting with all the panel lights flashing on and off, or staying illuminated, solved only by doing a hard reset or unplugging the unit for 5 minutes and trying again. The unit is very nice looking and relatively quiet. This unit seems to be one of the lower priced dishwashers which is attractive if on a tight budget however it does feel less expensive as well, trays are lightweight and not as smooth rolling in and out as more expensive dishwashers. At this point we don't press any other buttons than leaving it in the normal wash mode, pressing the on button, and the start buttonm and then we stay away until it finishes washing. Maybe the other buttons would work for different wash cycles however that initially led to hours of frustration so we use it in the simplest manner possible. The APP does signal when a cycle successfully completes which is reassuring but we don't use it for anything in order to avoid recreating the frozen front panel situation.

Sentence (English): Warning: Unless you own and exclusively wash a perfect set of Corelle Ware dishes only, do not purchase this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Not recommended ] || ---------------- || Warning: Unless you own and exclusively wash a perfect set of Corelle Ware dishes only, do not purchase this dishwasher. This is the first 1-star rating I have ever written on anything, so I do not take this lightly. I really wanted to love this dishwasher, but it has proven to be the worst design I have encountered in a dishwasher. After more than 40 years' experience loading dishwashers, I believe I know how to load one, but this design requires loading of only uniform and shallow dishes, with nothing made of plastic. My main motivation for purchasing this dishwasher was to use only the upper drawer most of the time, thus avoiding bending over to load and unload it, as is necessary with standard dishwashers. I also hoped to eliminate the need to handwash any dishes. Neither of my desires have been met. The rack in each drawer is the same design with the left side of the rack oddly slanted for no obvious reason, making the loading of bowls with any depth a frustrating challenge. Although the tines on this side can be adjusted to create wider spaces, this adjustment does not resolve the issue. The right-side tines are intended for plates, but they are too tall and positioned too narrowly for a plate with any width. While these tines can be folded flat to accommodate other dishware, doing so means there is no space left for plates. The manual suggests an ideal loading scenario, but it is clear from the images that ONLY Corelle Ware-type dishes fit this rack. Additionally, when washing lightweight items such as Tupperware bowls, they frequently flip over and then collect water. This trapped water creates humidity, thus preventing the dishes from drying completely even on the longest dry cycle. The upper fold-down racks are ineffective because placing any dishware beneath them obstructs water flow. There is also a risk of items falling below the rack, which can block the water sprayer and result in dishes not being cleaned properly. I sincerely regret purchasing this dishwasher!

However, the "door open" feature for drying can't be beat, love that normal cleaning time is only 1 hr. 30 min. and the overall cleaning is fantastic. We contacted Maytag and informed that it wasn't their problem. We explained it had come directly from them and we had a defective dishwasher. Again, not their problem. Sentence (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.
