Sentence (English): Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household?
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): So, I decided on the 6-person model.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): It also uses much less water than washing by hand.
Comments (English): I am someone who finds washing dishes a real hassle. Because of my personality, I can't just do things haphazardly, so it takes me at least an hour to wash dishes even after a single meal. It takes even longer when there is a lot of food or greasy dishes, and I use a lot of hot water. That is why I have always wanted to buy a dishwasher. I was very satisfied with a 3-person dishwasher I bought secondhand for 100,000 won a long time ago, but I regretted selling it after moving to a house with a smaller kitchen. After moving, I had plenty of extra space, so I spent a long time debating whether to buy a 3-person or a 6-person model. Do I really need a 6-person one for a single-person household? However, based on my past experience, the 3-person model was a tight fit for even a single double-handled pot, and I had to carefully squeeze knives or cutting boards in due to their length, or couldn't fit them at all. So, I decided on the 6-person model. Although I measured the dimensions while choosing the installation location, it looks too big in person. I think I didn't get a sense of its size from the photos because they lacked depth. So, every time I see it taking up a large corner of the kitchen, I regret not buying a smaller one. However, it is nice that it is large when you put various items in to wash dishes. Also, it is good that the plate holder on the left side of the interior is foldable. When putting in small dishes, I think it is best to place them upside down in the middle. I placed a small bowl upside down in the corner near the entrance, and none of them got cleaned. Come to think of it, since the bowl is shallow and placed upside down, the water jets sprayed from the side probably didn't reach it. I think it would have been better to just tilt it. It is a bit disappointing that this product lacks a hot air drying function. However, since dishes are dried while still wet even when hand-washed, it is not a major drawback. That said, the air doesn't circulate well inside the dishwasher, so it feels like the dishes aren't drying as thoroughly; therefore, I usually leave the door wide open. Those who want dishes that are perfectly clean and dry might not be satisfied with this product. However, if it had a hot air drying function, the longer operating time might actually cause some inconvenience. The sound of the water splashing and the drainage operation can be quite loud if you pay attention to it, but I think it would be fine once you get used to it and don't consciously think about it. I was worried that cleaning would be a hassle if food got stuck inside the dishwasher, so I rinse off the food residue as a pre-wash before putting the dishes in. That is a bit of a hassle, but it is bearable. It has only been three days since I installed it, so its large size is still a bit of a burden, but I really like the convenience of dishwashing. I love being able to use multiple dishes without worrying about washing them. In particular, I can use knives, scissors (because I'm afraid of tearing holes in rubber gloves), container lids, forks, and tongs without worry. If you calculate the hourly wage of washing dishes every day, buying a dishwasher is much more cost-effective. It also uses much less water than washing by hand. If anyone is debating whether to buy one, I highly recommend it.

Sentence (English): Okay let's start off and say that i love everything costco.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher, Horrible service + rust ] || ---------------- || Okay let's start off and say that i love everything costco. I've gotten my refrigerator and mattress (amongst other things) from it, and I'm a big fan. So when I got my maytag dishwasher from them, I was pumped. I got it back in June '25, and by Nov/Dec '25, BAM! Rust begins to form right above the steam vent on the dishwasher. I'm thinking to myself “This can't be true, it's only a 6 month old unit! ”. So I call costco technical and warranty support to get some help with this. After a good amount of emailing back and forth (with photos), plus some lengthy and frustrating phone calls, I get told that in fact thousands of people are dealing with the same issue on their stainless steel maytag dishwashers….drum roll….due to hard water. If it's due to hard water, then why didn't this happen to my last dishwasher? Or any of my stainless steel pans? I'm given a $50 costco credit for the trouble and told they can't do anything else. So i'm just supposed to wait for the rust to spread? If it's visible that the clear coat on the washer isn't working and is defective, doesn't that mean a replacement or even return is in order? So if you're thinking of buying this and you live in california, the bay area, or ANYWHERE that has “hard water”, which sounds like everywhere…well, think again.

Sentence (English): Writing this review after two months of use for the Bosch 500 series, and so far everything is great.
Comments (English): [ It Washes Dishes ] || ---------------- || Writing this review after two months of use for the Bosch 500 series, and so far everything is great. After having bought other, cheaper dishwashers from other brands, I've come to realize that it's a high bar to ask for a dishwasher to actually do what its name implies-- that is, to wash dishes. And the Bosch does. How delightfully refreshing. Yes, the price tag is higher than other brands (and for that matter, the 100 or 300 series from Bosch itself). But as any middle-aged adult of the modern era has come to discover, you apparently have to pay a premium for an appliance to actually function. Personally speaking, I live in a rural area where it is difficult, if not impossible, to get repairs done, so it's important that I have a reliable machine. So far, so good. Some basic notes on this model: * Other reviews have commented on the design/ functionality of the interior racks, but for me it does the job. There is no ideal setup for the various dishes people use, so all told this one works just fine. * The "Auto-Air" function is great: this is where the dishwasher automatically opens to finish the drying process. It appears to save a lot of energy that normally would be spent on a heating unit, and the dishes are plenty dry afterwards. Keep in mind that the 100 and 300 series (and the Costco version of the 500) do not have this feature, but it is well worth it. * It is true that some functions of the dishwasher require you to use the app. The app is fairly intuitive, so that didn't create a problem for me. And, once you create some basic settings, you can simply start the dishwasher from the unit itself (although a delay wash does need the app). * CONS: the delay wash requires you to use the app. It would have been great to include this on the unit itself, since the last thing I want to do after loading the dishwasher is to ask my phone if it's ok to do the dishes. But again, not a deal-breaker. Overall, a great machine, and time will tell if it's as reliable as advertised.

Sentence (English): - 3-Month Review.
Comments (English): [ Serves 1-2! If not reheat immediately after eating, burnt-on cannot be cleaned. ] || ---------------- || - 3-Month Review. Purchased on 1/29, Review dated 5/7. I checked through the window to see if it was cleaning properly, and the water doesn't reach the cutlery area. For that price, it's worth buying for a Kugase... but the cleaning power is just too disappointing. Even though it is powerful, it doesn't clean well without a pre-wash. The more I use it, the more disappointed I am. -----------------------------------------------------. Reason for Purchase: I bought this because washing dishes is a hassle and I felt like I was wasting too much water. Installation: I intended to place it next to the sink, but I didn't consider the space needed to open the door, so opening it to the side as shown in the photo is actually more convenient. Design: The white tone matches the kitchen well and gives a clean look. The size isn't overwhelming, so it's good to use even in small spaces. Usage: It fits about 1 to 2 servings at a time. If you put cups, plates, and cutlery together, it fits quite generously. Cleaning Power: It cleans most greasy dishes well. I was satisfied that glass cups and dishes came out clean with almost no water stains (as shown in the photo). It is better to rinse any leftover residue on cutlery or completely burnt-on food before putting them in. Pros: - Decent size for a dishwasher. - Better-than-expected cleaning power. - Reduces the effort of washing dishes. - Minimal water stains. Cons: - Residue may occasionally remain in the deep parts of cutlery. - Takes a long time to dry completely. Overall: This is a sufficiently satisfactory product for reducing dishwashing stress while living alone. I think it is a good value choice, especially for those living alone or in a two-person household.

Sentence (English): My family has traditionally bought all Samsung electronics.
Comments (English): My family has traditionally bought all Samsung electronics. However, I bought a dishwasher this time because I wanted to try out an LG product. But looking at how LG handles things, it feels like something is missing. First of all, this is a built-in model. I replaced my old Samsung dishwasher, but I ended up having to install it because there is no baseboard. In the case of Samsung, they check for things like baseboards to ensure installation is possible before proceeding with the installation process. LG, however, just installed the dishwasher and left. At the very least, they should have said, "Since there is no baseboard, please contact our LG Electronics renovation company." When I asked the installer how to handle the baseboard and if they had a partner company, they replied that they didn't know (even though there are partner companies listed on their website). Would they install a dishwasher in their own home and treat customers like that? The user experience is truly terrible. No matter how good LG products are, I think I will avoid them because of this kind of user experience.

Sentence (English): This is the 3rd GE Profile dishwasher I've owned in the last 17 years.
Comments (English): [ Works, but not as well as past models ] || ---------------- || This is the 3rd GE Profile dishwasher I've owned in the last 17 years. The first one was great, but I moved shortly after upgrading our kitchen appliances. I like it so much that I purchased a new one for the new house. It lasted nearly 12 years and ran perfectly up until it finally broke. This latest one is nowhere near as good as the others. Half the time the dishwasher pods don't completely come out the soap container. We use the same pods that came with the dishwasher, so it's not a pod issue. At least once week we get dishes that still have stuff caked on them. I never know when it runs out of the Jet-Dry. My last GE Profile had actual displays for things like this. When it works, it works well and is nice and quiet. I also like having notifications on my phone for when it's done running. It's frustrating to see the decline in quality and will likely look for an alternate brand next time around.

Sentence (English): I installed the dishwasher myself as I did a Bosch years ago.
Comments (English): [ Cleans Very well ] || ---------------- || I installed the dishwasher myself as I did a Bosch years ago. The first thing I noticed is the unit had 1" of fiber insulation draped over the unit like half a sock on a foot. As expected the unit was hard to get the insulation and machine in the space allotted for the dishwasher. The dishwasher also came with some aluminum tape with no instructions on where to use it. After googling possible uses, I found that it was to be put above the opening of the cabinet to prevent water vapors from warping a wooden countertop. If you have a wooden counter i would use good flashing to prevent damage. The back 2 Leveling feet had to be adjusted before installation as there is no access after installation. The Bosch has a front adjuster for the back feet. The front foot panel had 2" thickness of the insulation that had to be tape in place so I could install the front toe kick plate. Instructions warn not to let the insulation hit the float switch. There is no way to know after the plate goes up. Just pointing out petty quality issues. The dishwasher cleaned on normal cycle very well. Letting the door pop open, aids to the drying process a lot. I bought the Kitchen Aid because the washing parts are all stainless steel. The Bosch has plastic rotating parts.

Sentence (English): We purchased this unit when out Whirlpool 2019 gave out.
Comments (English): [ Cleans Well, but Not Good Design ] || ---------------- || We purchased this unit when out Whirlpool 2019 gave out. I wanted a unit where the filter could be changed easily. Compared to the old Whirlpool, this KitchenAid cleans much better (probably because I could NOT access the Whirlpool's filter to clean it). The interior design; however, is worse. Stemware does not really fit well anywhere in the upper rack and there are no hooks/guards to secure wine glasses. Additionally, the prongs are weirdly spaced and allows drinking glasses, small plates and bowls to fall sideways. This is also the problem with the lower rack. Plates only fit securely when lined up in the middle prongs. This reduces loading space and requires you to either load plates in other prongs where they roll back and forth, or run a semi-full load. I also miss having upper and lower fold down rows to accommodate larger dishes. The KitchenAid only has stationary rows of prongs. The silverware basket is ok, but less capacity than the Whirlpool. I actually use my old Whirlpool silverware basket in my KitchenAid because I like the room it offers. The very upper flatware rack is good and accommodates larger serving pieces and knives. Is it enough to be a game changer. probably not. The exterior design is good. The touch pad is easy to use and there are ample washing cycles to support most needs. Overall, I would not purchase a KitchenAid again unless these issues were fixed. I would repurchase a Whirlpool again, only if the filter was easier to access and clean. Yes, I realize these two brands are owned by the same company. Maybe they can produce a hybrid of the two units to give us the ultimate in dishwashers! With all of this said, I am glad I was able to get a dishwasher to replace my old non-functioning one.

In the past, I often avoided cooking at home because washing dishes was such a hassle. The cooking itself was fine, but seeing the pile of dishes after the meal felt like a burden. I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

In the past, I often avoided cooking at home because washing dishes was such a hassle. The cooking itself was fine, but seeing the pile of dishes after the meal felt like a burden. In the past, I would simply order delivery or eat out because of the thought of washing dishes, but now I just cook, neatly stack the dishes, and run the cycle, so the burden has been significantly reduced. After a meal, I roughly organize the dishes and put them away; once a certain amount has accumulated, I just add detergent and run the cycle—it's not very inconvenient. At first, I thought organizing the dishes might be a hassle, but once I got used to it, it actually felt much more convenient than washing by hand. What I particularly liked was that the noise level is lower than I anticipated. At first, I was worried that the dishwasher might be quite noisy when running, but after actually using it, the noise level was comparable to everyday sounds and wasn't particularly bothersome. It is quiet enough that I don't really notice it even when I'm doing other things or relaxing at home, so I am quite satisfied with this aspect. In terms of cleaning power, most dishes after a typical meal are cleaned thoroughly. Rice bowls, plates, and cups usually come out clean without needing any special attention. In cases where food had completely dried and stuck on like a cake, the dishwasher alone could not remove it completely. In such cases, it was better to simply soak them in water or smooth them out by hand before putting them in. Nevertheless, I was quite satisfied just knowing that it takes care of most of the dishwashing for me. Even if it doesn't solve everything 100%, the significant reduction in the burden of dishwashing is something I can really feel. Personally, I felt that this issue was more influenced by the detergent or usage method than by a problem with the product itself. The noise level is quieter than expected. Personally, this product made me understand why dishwashers are referred to as the "three great home appliances." I am leaving this review in case anyone is struggling with the burden of washing dishes and wants to give this a try. I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

In the past, I often avoided cooking at home because washing dishes was such a hassle. The cooking itself was fine, but seeing the pile of dishes after the meal felt like a burden. In the past, I would simply order delivery or eat out because of the thought of washing dishes, but now I just cook, neatly stack the dishes, and run the cycle, so the burden has been significantly reduced. After a meal, I roughly organize the dishes and put them away; once a certain amount has accumulated, I just add detergent and run the cycle—it's not very inconvenient. At first, I thought organizing the dishes might be a hassle, but once I got used to it, it actually felt much more convenient than washing by hand. What I particularly liked was that the noise level is lower than I anticipated. At first, I was worried that the dishwasher might be quite noisy when running, but after actually using it, the noise level was comparable to everyday sounds and wasn't particularly bothersome. It is quiet enough that I don't really notice it even when I'm doing other things or relaxing at home, so I am quite satisfied with this aspect. In terms of cleaning power, most dishes after a typical meal are cleaned thoroughly. Rice bowls, plates, and cups usually come out clean without needing any special attention. Even greasy dishes are cleaned better than expected, so I have come to leave most of my daily dishwashing to the dishwasher. However, not all food residue is perfectly removed. In cases where food had completely dried and stuck on like a cake, the dishwasher alone could not remove it completely. In such cases, it was better to simply soak them in water or smooth them out by hand before putting them in. Nevertheless, I was quite satisfied just knowing that it takes care of most of the dishwashing for me. Even if it doesn't solve everything 100%, the significant reduction in the burden of dishwashing is something I can really feel. Personally, I felt that this issue was more influenced by the detergent or usage method than by a problem with the product itself. To summarize my overall impressions after using it: The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced. I find myself cooking home-cooked meals much more often. It is easy to use. The noise level is quieter than expected. Personally, this product made me understand why dishwashers are referred to as the "three great home appliances." I am leaving this review in case anyone is struggling with the burden of washing dishes and wants to give this a try. I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

In the past, I often avoided cooking at home because washing dishes was such a hassle. The cooking itself was fine, but seeing the pile of dishes after the meal felt like a burden. In terms of cleaning power, most dishes after a typical meal are cleaned thoroughly. Rice bowls, plates, and cups usually come out clean without needing any special attention. In cases where food had completely dried and stuck on like a cake, the dishwasher alone could not remove it completely. In such cases, it was better to simply soak them in water or smooth them out by hand before putting them in. Even if it doesn't solve everything 100%, the significant reduction in the burden of dishwashing is something I can really feel.
