I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

In the past, I often avoided cooking at home because washing dishes was such a hassle. The cooking itself was fine, but seeing the pile of dishes after the meal felt like a burden. I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

In the past, I often avoided cooking at home because washing dishes was such a hassle. The cooking itself was fine, but seeing the pile of dishes after the meal felt like a burden. After much consideration, I decided to get a Samsung 6-place dishwasher, and now that I've used it, I understand why so many people recommend them. In the past, I would simply order delivery or eat out because of the thought of washing dishes, but now I just cook, neatly stack the dishes, and run the cycle, so the burden has been significantly reduced. The usage is also simpler than I expected. After a meal, I roughly organize the dishes and put them away; once a certain amount has accumulated, I just add detergent and run the cycle—it's not very inconvenient. At first, I thought organizing the dishes might be a hassle, but once I got used to it, it actually felt much more convenient than washing by hand. What I particularly liked was that the noise level is lower than I anticipated. At first, I was worried that the dishwasher might be quite noisy when running, but after actually using it, the noise level was comparable to everyday sounds and wasn't particularly bothersome. It is quiet enough that I don't really notice it even when I'm doing other things or relaxing at home, so I am quite satisfied with this aspect. In terms of cleaning power, most dishes after a typical meal are cleaned thoroughly. Rice bowls, plates, and cups usually come out clean without needing any special attention. Even greasy dishes are cleaned better than expected, so I have come to leave most of my daily dishwashing to the dishwasher. However, not all food residue is perfectly removed. In cases where food had completely dried and stuck on like a cake, the dishwasher alone could not remove it completely. In such cases, it was better to simply soak them in water or smooth them out by hand before putting them in. Nevertheless, I was quite satisfied just knowing that it takes care of most of the dishwashing for me. Even if it doesn't solve everything 100%, the significant reduction in the burden of dishwashing is something I can really feel. Another thing I realized is that choosing the right detergent is also important. When I first used it, perhaps because I chose the wrong detergent, there were times when it smelled a bit fishy. So, I thought it would be better to try changing the detergent or paying a little more attention to maintenance. Personally, I felt that this issue was more influenced by the detergent or usage method than by a problem with the product itself. To summarize my overall impressions after using it: The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced. I find myself cooking home-cooked meals much more often. It is easy to use. The noise level is quieter than expected. Of course, there are times when you still need to manually clean up completely dried food residue, but even with just these aspects, I felt it was a sufficiently satisfying product. Personally, this product made me understand why dishwashers are referred to as the "three great home appliances." I am leaving this review in case anyone is struggling with the burden of washing dishes and wants to give this a try. I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

In the past, I often avoided cooking at home because washing dishes was such a hassle. The cooking itself was fine, but seeing the pile of dishes after the meal felt like a burden. After much consideration, I decided to get a Samsung 6-place dishwasher, and now that I've used it, I understand why so many people recommend them. The biggest change I've noticed is that I cook at home much more frequently. In the past, I would simply order delivery or eat out because of the thought of washing dishes, but now I just cook, neatly stack the dishes, and run the cycle, so the burden has been significantly reduced. The usage is also simpler than I expected. After a meal, I roughly organize the dishes and put them away; once a certain amount has accumulated, I just add detergent and run the cycle—it's not very inconvenient. At first, I thought organizing the dishes might be a hassle, but once I got used to it, it actually felt much more convenient than washing by hand. What I particularly liked was that the noise level is lower than I anticipated. At first, I was worried that the dishwasher might be quite noisy when running, but after actually using it, the noise level was comparable to everyday sounds and wasn't particularly bothersome. It is quiet enough that I don't really notice it even when I'm doing other things or relaxing at home, so I am quite satisfied with this aspect. In terms of cleaning power, most dishes after a typical meal are cleaned thoroughly. Rice bowls, plates, and cups usually come out clean without needing any special attention. Even greasy dishes are cleaned better than expected, so I have come to leave most of my daily dishwashing to the dishwasher. However, not all food residue is perfectly removed. In cases where food had completely dried and stuck on like a cake, the dishwasher alone could not remove it completely. In such cases, it was better to simply soak them in water or smooth them out by hand before putting them in. Nevertheless, I was quite satisfied just knowing that it takes care of most of the dishwashing for me. Even if it doesn't solve everything 100%, the significant reduction in the burden of dishwashing is something I can really feel. Another thing I realized is that choosing the right detergent is also important. When I first used it, perhaps because I chose the wrong detergent, there were times when it smelled a bit fishy. So, I thought it would be better to try changing the detergent or paying a little more attention to maintenance. Personally, I felt that this issue was more influenced by the detergent or usage method than by a problem with the product itself. To summarize my overall impressions after using it: The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced. I find myself cooking home-cooked meals much more often. It is easy to use. The noise level is quieter than expected. Of course, there are times when you still need to manually clean up completely dried food residue, but even with just these aspects, I felt it was a sufficiently satisfying product. Personally, this product made me understand why dishwashers are referred to as the "three great home appliances." I am leaving this review in case anyone is struggling with the burden of washing dishes and wants to give this a try. I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

In the past, I often avoided cooking at home because washing dishes was such a hassle. The cooking itself was fine, but seeing the pile of dishes after the meal felt like a burden. After much consideration, I decided to get a Samsung 6-place dishwasher, and now that I've used it, I understand why so many people recommend them. The biggest change I've noticed is that I cook at home much more frequently. In the past, I would simply order delivery or eat out because of the thought of washing dishes, but now I just cook, neatly stack the dishes, and run the cycle, so the burden has been significantly reduced. The usage is also simpler than I expected. After a meal, I roughly organize the dishes and put them away; once a certain amount has accumulated, I just add detergent and run the cycle—it's not very inconvenient. At first, I thought organizing the dishes might be a hassle, but once I got used to it, it actually felt much more convenient than washing by hand. What I particularly liked was that the noise level is lower than I anticipated. At first, I was worried that the dishwasher might be quite noisy when running, but after actually using it, the noise level was comparable to everyday sounds and wasn't particularly bothersome. It is quiet enough that I don't really notice it even when I'm doing other things or relaxing at home, so I am quite satisfied with this aspect. In terms of cleaning power, most dishes after a typical meal are cleaned thoroughly. Rice bowls, plates, and cups usually come out clean without needing any special attention. Even greasy dishes are cleaned better than expected, so I have come to leave most of my daily dishwashing to the dishwasher. However, not all food residue is perfectly removed. In cases where food had completely dried and stuck on like a cake, the dishwasher alone could not remove it completely. In such cases, it was better to simply soak them in water or smooth them out by hand before putting them in. Nevertheless, I was quite satisfied just knowing that it takes care of most of the dishwashing for me. Even if it doesn't solve everything 100%, the significant reduction in the burden of dishwashing is something I can really feel. Another thing I realized is that choosing the right detergent is also important. When I first used it, perhaps because I chose the wrong detergent, there were times when it smelled a bit fishy. So, I thought it would be better to try changing the detergent or paying a little more attention to maintenance. Personally, I felt that this issue was more influenced by the detergent or usage method than by a problem with the product itself. To summarize my overall impressions after using it: The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced. I find myself cooking home-cooked meals much more often. It is easy to use. The noise level is quieter than expected. Of course, there are times when you still need to manually clean up completely dried food residue, but even with just these aspects, I felt it was a sufficiently satisfying product. Personally, this product made me understand why dishwashers are referred to as the "three great home appliances." I am leaving this review in case anyone is struggling with the burden of washing dishes and wants to give this a try. I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

In the past, I often avoided cooking at home because washing dishes was such a hassle. The cooking itself was fine, but seeing the pile of dishes after the meal felt like a burden. After much consideration, I decided to get a Samsung 6-place dishwasher, and now that I've used it, I understand why so many people recommend them. The biggest change I've noticed is that I cook at home much more frequently. In the past, I would simply order delivery or eat out because of the thought of washing dishes, but now I just cook, neatly stack the dishes, and run the cycle, so the burden has been significantly reduced. The usage is also simpler than I expected. After a meal, I roughly organize the dishes and put them away; once a certain amount has accumulated, I just add detergent and run the cycle—it's not very inconvenient. At first, I thought organizing the dishes might be a hassle, but once I got used to it, it actually felt much more convenient than washing by hand. What I particularly liked was that the noise level is lower than I anticipated. At first, I was worried that the dishwasher might be quite noisy when running, but after actually using it, the noise level was comparable to everyday sounds and wasn't particularly bothersome. It is quiet enough that I don't really notice it even when I'm doing other things or relaxing at home, so I am quite satisfied with this aspect. In terms of cleaning power, most dishes after a typical meal are cleaned thoroughly. Rice bowls, plates, and cups usually come out clean without needing any special attention. Even greasy dishes are cleaned better than expected, so I have come to leave most of my daily dishwashing to the dishwasher. However, not all food residue is perfectly removed. In cases where food had completely dried and stuck on like a cake, the dishwasher alone could not remove it completely. In such cases, it was better to simply soak them in water or smooth them out by hand before putting them in. Nevertheless, I was quite satisfied just knowing that it takes care of most of the dishwashing for me. Even if it doesn't solve everything 100%, the significant reduction in the burden of dishwashing is something I can really feel. Another thing I realized is that choosing the right detergent is also important. When I first used it, perhaps because I chose the wrong detergent, there were times when it smelled a bit fishy. So, I thought it would be better to try changing the detergent or paying a little more attention to maintenance. Personally, I felt that this issue was more influenced by the detergent or usage method than by a problem with the product itself. To summarize my overall impressions after using it: The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced. I find myself cooking home-cooked meals much more often. It is easy to use. The noise level is quieter than expected. Of course, there are times when you still need to manually clean up completely dried food residue, but even with just these aspects, I felt it was a sufficiently satisfying product. Personally, this product made me understand why dishwashers are referred to as the "three great home appliances." I am leaving this review in case anyone is struggling with the burden of washing dishes and wants to give this a try. I think satisfaction will be particularly high for those who cook home-cooked meals frequently, just like me.

Sentence (English): When we were setting up our new home as newlyweds, we didn't install a dishwasher because we wondered if it was really necessary.
Comments (English): [ It's the best. ] || ---------------- || When we were setting up our new home as newlyweds, we didn't install a dishwasher because we wondered if it was really necessary. However, every time we invited guests over and faced the massive pile of dishes, I would just sigh in frustration. It was a huge waste of water and detergent, and above all, the chore of washing dishes after a long day at work was exhausting. Then, I came across a great special offer and purchased and installed a Samsung dishwasher. Now that I’ve used it myself, I feel like I can never go back to the days when I didn't have one. Being a 14-place setting model, the interior space is much more spacious, making it easy to load pots and large bowls at once. The height of the top basket is also freely adjustable, making storage efficiency excellent. The burden of cleaning up after cooking has been drastically reduced, and it has completely changed my mindset when I step into the kitchen. I am also extremely satisfied with its performance. Perhaps thanks to the 4-stage 3D water jets, even a quick pre-wash removes grease stains, leaving everything squeaky clean, which is incredibly satisfying. I particularly love that the door opens automatically after the cycle is finished, allowing the dishes to dry cleanly without any musty water smell. Since it has a Grade 1 energy efficiency rating, the electricity bill is low even if I run it every day, and because the noise is barely noticeable, I feel at ease using it late at night. Buying a dishwasher feels less like simply adding another appliance and more like purchasing the "value of time." The greatest happiness is having the luxury of enjoying a cup of coffee instead of doing the dishes. If anyone is hesitating like I was, I highly recommend this. It is a true revolution and an essential item for my kitchen.

(Not literally - it just doesn't work.) It just takes up space without being functional. (See my previous comments about loading utensils there.)-The shelves themselves are finnicky when trying to load. There is no tactile response when trying to select cycle or options so you have to wait until a light pops up (or not) before knowing if your selection was accepted. Even with experience, it takes a bit of time/effort and appropriate bodily gestures to get things selected and started. OK. Real life experience. I rarely write reviews except when things really run counter to expectations - whether positive or negative. This experience has been WAAAY negative. Again, my recommendation: don't buy this dishwasher.

I rarely write reviews except when things really run counter to expectations - whether positive or negative. This experience has been WAAAY negative. Again, my recommendation: don't buy this dishwasher.
